name: AuxPair.conjKernel_equivariant
summary: conjKernel is the conjugate of a theta value; moving k through the datum costs levelChar(k)^(-1) = conj(levelChar(k)) (pairWeil_fockDatum), and the rational gamma is absorbed by the invariance of theta under rational points.

steps.claim: Compare the theta values before complex conjugation, in two steps.
steps.lean:
k • (stdSpace ..).weightRep _ O.detExp γ v) = O.conjKernel g x v := congrArg star (.trans (by
  simpa [← pairTheta_mul, ↓Complex.inv_eq_conj (LevelPlaces.isOfFinOrder_level_char k).norm_eq_one,
    map_inv, Prod.mul_def] using! congr(pairTheta _ _ O.a O.b $(O.pairWeil_fockDatum _ k⁻¹ _) (_, 1,
    _ * k)).symm) (O.pairThetaKernel.swap.theta_rat_mul _ ⟨_, rfl⟩ _))

steps.claim: Moving k: omega(1, (1, k^(-1))) sends the datum at conj xi to levelChar(O)(k^(-1)) times the datum at conj(conjWeylRep(kappa(O), detExp(O))(1)(xi)) = conj xi (pairWeil_fockDatum), and levelChar(O)(k) has absolute value 1, so its inverse is its conjugate; this cancels the factor levelChar(O)(k) of the argument.
steps.lean:
(by
  simpa [← pairTheta_mul, ↓Complex.inv_eq_conj (LevelPlaces.isOfFinOrder_level_char k).norm_eq_one,
    map_inv, Prod.mul_def] using! congr(pairTheta _ _ O.a O.b $(O.pairWeil_fockDatum _ k⁻¹ _) (_, 1,
    _ * k)).symm)

steps.claim: The theta functional is invariant under the rational point gamma of U(I_n)(E).
